name: amp-offset-sensitivity
description: Issue #42 (bench created by #10): measured dVref/dVos with a small offset source inserted in series in the amp's in_n path (electrically identical to an amp input-referred offset), verifying the error budget's amp-offset sensitivity line (design/bandgap_error_budget.md Sec 2) against the real closed loop. Re-run against the telescopic-cascode amp to confirm the redesign did not move this core-determined number.
claim: design/bandgap_error_budget.md Sec 2 (amp input-referred offset -> Vref sensitivity line); not a ratified spec line.

dvref_dvos.description: Sanity bound around the R1/R2-based Brokaw-gain estimate (magnitude ~15.28, design/bandgap_operating_point.md Sec 2; also consistent with the ~14.3 gain figure derived independently in spec/decision-records/0003-target-spec-ratification.md's spec-review input): the measured closed-loop sensitivity should land in the same order of magnitude at every corner. Sign is POSITIVE, not negative as a first guess from the R1/R2 magnitude alone might suggest: in_n = vos_node = sns1 + vos increases with vos, and this amp's in_n is the inverting input for its own output (see design/bandgap_amp.sch's M1/M2/M3/M4 topology -- M1's drain is the diode-referenced mirror node, M2's drain is the high-impedance output node, so increasing in_n pulls the amp's output/fb node down), which decreases the PMOS mirror Vsg headroom the wrong way -- i.e. fb falling *increases* every core mirror leg's current, and Vref = VEB(Q3) + I*R1 is dominated by the I*R1 term, so higher I means higher Vref. Net: dVref/dVos is positive. Not a ratified spec line -- see design/bandgap_error_budget.md Sec 2 for how this feeds the offset budget and Sec 4 for the loop's sign convention.
